source.title: Towards Demystifying the Generalization Behaviors When Neural Collapse Emerges
source.authors: Pei-Feng Gao; Qian-Qian Xu; Yi-Bo Yang; Pei-Song Wen; Huiyang Shao; Zhi-Yong Yang; Bernard Ghanem; Qing-Ming Huang

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training and test results on generalization during neural collapse, using margin and feature alignment analyses. Its experiments do not test the claim versions’ specified comparisons directly.
record.gate_note: The study measures training margin during terminal-phase training and test accuracy and cross-entropy under different classifier rotations and permutations. It does not test random-label fitting, width sweeps, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The study tests margin growth during neural-collapse training and sensitivity of test performance to classifier permutations and rotations. These are different questions from V1–V8. Feature-dimension comparisons do not establish V2's width effect beyond interpolation; margin bounds do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure. Removing dropout throughout the recipe supplies no dropout comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors interpret increasing margins and their multiclass margin bound as explaining test improvement during terminal-phase training, and report sensitivity of test performance to fixed-classifier permutations and rotations despite perfect training accuracy. Their own margin experiment verifies margin growth; the cited empirical evidence for test improvement over terminal-phase training comes from Papyan et al. (2020). The bound supplies a theoretical explanation rather than a demonstrated guarantee of improving test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a neural-collapse setup with a fixed, simplex-ETF-initialized classifier and varies permutation or rotation; this is not a direct reproduction of the claim versions’ stated experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Test performance varied with the classifier’s initial permutation or rotation; reported for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 using three convolutional backbones and two feature dimensions per dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the six backbone–dataset combinations, minimum training logit margin increases as cross-entropy approaches zero during terminal-phase training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Minimum training margin can continue increasing after training accuracy reaches 100%.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report differing test accuracies and test cross-entropies across fixed-classifier permutations and rotations despite perfect training classification. For d<C, the classifier structures are obtained by unconstrained-feature optimization rather than simplex ETFs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classifier orientation and class assignment can affect held-out performance in fixed-classifier neural-collapse training.

record.problems: Permutation and rotation comparisons are shown in figures without numeric result values or reported uncertainty estimates in the text. The experiment uses a fixed classifier and controlled training seed, so it does not establish that the observed differences hold across ordinary unconstrained training recipes.
record.rows_left_out: The figures report test cross-entropy alongside accuracy for the same model, dataset, feature dimension, and transformation conditions. Those additional metric rows are omitted because the prose says they differ in Figure 5 but provides no separate text values, and the 60-row cap prioritizes the described accuracy results and margin results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Test-error changes as network width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes that recover large-batch performance.
Held-out effects of adding or removing dropout, including interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps and its ranking against alternative measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T2 is inappropriate because none of the specified versions is tested. The word significant in the results describes reported differences; the supplied text gives no significance test. All rows remain linked to none. The cannot_determine states concern the specified claim effects and do not negate the reported margin-growth observation.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-versus-random held-out comparison.
No network-width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
The study examines training margins and test performance, but not magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.operation_detail: Tracked minimum training margin pmin as cross-entropy decreased during terminal-phase training.
rows.value: The margin pmin keeps increasing as the CE loss approaches zero.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend; it does not provide numerical values in the text.
rows.check: The reported increasing-margin trend is supported by Section 5.1, but it measures none of V1–V8; observed cannot describe a claim-version effect.
